Consult Summary:
- Telehealth consult for 4-weeks postpartum woman with acute onset shortness of breath at rest with new nonproductive cough and palpitations; high concern for postpartum venous thromboembolism/pulmonary embolism; advised urgent hospital evaluation, patient to self-transport.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Sudden shortness of breath (SOB) at rest.
- Onset/duration: Began about 1 hour prior to call while sitting and watching TV.
- Course: Acute onset; patient uncertain if worsening. Reports feeling stressed/anxious with noticeable palpitations.
- Associated symptoms:
  - New cough since yesterday; nonproductive.
  - No chest pain; reports chest soreness with deep inspiration and tenderness around C-section scar.
  - Palpitations (“heart is really going”).
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No prior similar SOB episodes.
  - No sputum production.
  - No chest pain at rest.
  - Infant well; no illness in baby.
- Relevant context: Cesarean section 4 weeks ago; currently at home with newborn; alone at time of call (partner at work).

Past Medical History:
- Post-cesarean section (4 weeks postpartum).
- Denies other medical problems.

Medications:
- Codeine for post-op pain; taken fairly regularly after delivery but not taken for ~1 week (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Advised not to take codeine for now.
- Allergies: Ibuprofen (reaction not documented).

Social History:
- Postpartum; at home with infant; alone during call (partner at work).
- No tobacco, alcohol, or substance use history documented.

Family History:
- Mother with history of leg clots (venous thrombosis).

Physical Examination:
- Telehealth visit; no formal vitals recorded.
- Remote pulse check: Patient counted 30 beats over an unspecified interval; clinician assessed heart rate as “slightly fast.”

Investigations:
- None performed during consult.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute shortness of breath in 4-weeks postpartum patient, with tachycardia and new cough; concern for pulmonary embolism (postpartum/VTE risk).
  - Plan:
    - Urgent hospital evaluation recommended.
    - Option of ambulance offered; patient elected to self-transport promptly.
    - Advised to go quickly and bring supplies for baby.
    - Advised to avoid taking codeine for now.
    - Counseled on possible clot in lungs; hospital can provide treatment if confirmed.

- Issue 2: Postoperative pain/tenderness at C-section site.
  - Plan:
    - No new analgesia initiated during call; avoid codeine until evaluated in hospital.

- General Plan:
  - Patient agrees to plan and will proceed to the hospital now.

Quality checks (always include at bottom of note, or fill document_quality):
- Missing expected elements: Full vital signs; comprehensive ROS; full past medical/surgical history; obstetric details (e.g., pregnancy course, complications, prophylaxis); current medication list with doses/routes/frequencies; detailed allergy reaction; social history (tobacco/alcohol/substances); immunization status.
- Internal conflicts:
  - Date of birth stated as April 20, 1980 by patient; clinician restated “1983” (conflict noted).
  - When asked about other medical problems, patient said “Yeah” then “no” (conflict noted; ultimately denies other conditions).
- Transcript quality: Generally clear; minor pauses/ellipses; limited detail typical of urgent telehealth consult.
